name: GetVocal
one_line: GetVocal AI's voice, chat, WhatsApp and email agents for enterprise contact centres, built in its Agent Builder and supervised by people through its control console.

dims.question: What does the agent do on its own?

next_unlock.needs: Public evidence that agents operate across organisational boundaries or disparate stacks; and that others build on it: third parties publish integrations, skills or agents for it.

Public evidence that its limits and known failure cases are documented for those who use it.

gamma_ray.fact_ray: 20 facts: 20 π Moderate. Each is written beside its evidence above.
gamma_ray.built_from: GetVocal AI's own public product, blog, customer-story, privacy and status pages, and its published llms

configs.what: Agents built in Agent Builder and run on the platform with its defaults.
The customer's operators set which steps need a person's validation, approval or consultation before the agent proceeds.
The deployment opens each conversation by saying the customer is speaking with a virtual assistant; seen in one deployment, not stated as a default.

configs.config: Several agents in the Control Center
configs.what: The customer runs several agents, with conversations routed between them.

facts.label: It works across several domains or systems
facts.fact: The llms.txt says the agents work across the customer's CRM, CCaaS, telephony and helpdesk systems.
facts.quote: Agents handle voice and chat across your existing stack (CRM, CCaaS, telephony, helpdesk)

facts.label: The agent works independently; the person approves critical decisions only
facts.fact: The Control Tower page says the agent asks a human to approve critical decisions before executing them.
facts.quote: AI proactively asks a human to approve critical decisions before executing them.

facts.label: It connects to external tools or services across a trust boundary
facts.fact: The handoff payload is described as sent over a REST API to the agent desktop, naming Genesys Cloud and Salesforce integrations.
facts.quote: delivered via bidirectional REST API to the unified agent desktop

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: llms.txt says high-stakes actions such as large transactions, high-value returns and sensitive data get human-in-the-loop approval. A GetVocal blog on escalation says operators configure, in the Control Tower's Operator View, which decision nodes require validation.
facts.quote: with human-in-the-loop approval on high-stakes actions

facts.label: Its purpose and permitted tasks are stated in writing
facts.fact: The llms.txt says the agents resolve customer conversations end to end inside the customer's business rules, with human approval on high-stakes actions; the Control Tower FAQ says the agent cannot take actions its graph does not contain.
facts.quote: Agents resolve customer conversations end to end while staying inside your business rules

facts.label: It tells the people it talks to that it is an AI
facts.fact: In one deployment for an unnamed large Spanish telecom operator, each call opened with a disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant. No GetVocal page states that agents disclose they are AI by default or documents a disclosure setting; the EU AI Act blog advises deployers to add a disclosure node.
facts.quote: clear disclosure that the caller was speaking with a virtual assistant

facts.label: The data it uses is described
facts.fact: The agents are described as grounded in the customer's call scripts, help documents, CRM records and past transcripts.
facts.quote: a living model of your call scripts, help docs, CRM records and past transcripts

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of GetVocal's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
